Suppose the head moderator has not been active for over a month. The system will detect this, remove the head moderator, and assign the next mod in line (sorted by moderation level and date of being added) head moderator status, unless that moderator has been inactive for a month as well, in which case yet another mod in line will get it and the inactive mod gets removed. In case there is no active alternative moderator within the last month, the subverse is up for grabs for anyone who wants to get it - first come first served.

This is essentially the same process as /v/subverserequest, but automated. The level of abuse will severely drop, as people are too eager to just request subverses with an inactive head mod while the other mods are still plenty active - granted, this is more an issue with the rules regarding subverse requests, which are ironed out in my idea.

Summary

Head mod has not been active for over a month --> Head mod removed.

Next highest ranked mod has not been active for over a month since detection of head mod inactivity --> Mod removed.

Next highest ranked mod has been active in the last month since detection of head mod inactivity --> Mod will become head mod.

No mod has been active in the last month since detection of head mod inactivity --> Subverse becomes modless and available for the first user to make himself mod.

Amendment 1

All moderators having been inactive for over a month are to be removed as moderator automatically.

This would account for the situation where, say, the third mod in line has been selected as new mod, while mods 4 through 7 (or whatever), mods with an even lower mod level than the ones that were removed, would stay as mods - which doesn't make any sense. See /u/pm_me_your_airbags his comment chain.
Regarding /v/subverserequest: an automated system to assign head moderator status to the next active moderator of the subverse in case the head moderator has been inactive for over a month.
